transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 11:15am UTC
Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Dr. Sarah Chen (Halo Head of ML), Mark Ruiz (Halo CTO), Priya Patel (Halo Platform)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood, i'll run quick intro then priya will do console walkthrough, uh, feel free to interrupt
[00:12] Dr. Chen: thanks, yeah excited to see per-route stuff, we've got two main routes — triage-assist and patient-summary — want to understand cost per route and latency at 95th
[00:28] Priya: cool, we'll start in the console, so this is the Usage Analytics page, you can see aggregate tokens, requests per minute, and then a split by model and route, it's updated on a 1m cadence, occasionally there is a small lag if we backfill
[00:48] Mark: is that per-tenant? can we slice by env (prod/stage)?
[00:55] Priya: yep, top-left filter lets you toggle env, region, and model version, and you can pin a filter as a saved view, we'll show per-route next
[01:20] Priya: navigating to Per-Route Dashboards — here you get a dedicated pane for each route, you can see tokens, avg latency, p95, error rates, and cost breakdowns; the cost column is derived from token counts, model selection and quantization profile
[01:45] Dr. Chen: can we see caching effects? like KV cache hit rate per route?
[01:52] Priya: yes there's a 'cache' tab, shows prefix cache hits, kv cashe — apologies, sometimes our transcriptions show typos — KV cache hit rate, estimated token savings, and how that maps to dollars saved per 1M requests
[02:15] Alex: just to add, we estimate cost saving both from caching and batching; the console shows estimated savings if you enable intelligent batching for that route
[02:30] Mark: what about model fallbacks? if dedicated capacity is full do requests route to hosted smaller model?
[02:36] Priya: good question. on the routing policy UI you can set a primary (dedicated) and fallbacks by priority or cost, you can configure percent split for canary, also automatic fallback when capacity is depleted, and you can set per-route SLA thresholds that influence routing
[03:00] Priya Patel (customer): how is cost computed when we have multiple model variants? e.g., quantized 4bit vs fp16?
[03:08] Priya (Redwood): cost is model-unit based. we assign model cost-per-token derived from runtime profile; quantized variants have a lower per-token unit and the console shows blended cost for mixed-traffic routes. you can also drill into a model and see per-token cost by seq_len buckets
[03:34] Dr. Chen: ok that's helpful. we need to show finance team per-route billing, can we export CSV?
[03:40] Priya: yes export CSVs are available for any dashboard; we also have an API endpoint to pull per-route aggregated metrics if you want to automate reports (link: https://console.redwood.ai/api/metrics - note: sample only)
[04:05] Mark: are the numbers near real-time? our billing needs daily granularity
[04:10] Alex: yes daily and hourly exports, and you can set retention windows; for POC we can give you a daily export for the two routes
[04:24] Priya: now onto Cost Breakdown tab — shows per-route breakdown: compute token cost, infra surcharge (for dedicated), cache savings, and an estimated end-to-end cost per 1k requests, there's a slider to simulate traffic and model mix
[04:46] Dr. Chen: I noticed the console shows a 'cold-start' penalty for on-prem/private — where does that come from?
[04:53] Priya: that's from model loading times; private deployments can have warm pools but if you configure low replica count you'll see a cold-start multiplier; the console simulates this in the cost model
[05:10] Mark: security: we need KMS integration and audit logs, are those available?
[05:16] Alex: yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for private deployments; hosted keys are optional. audit logs surface auth events, API calls, model loads. we'll attach SOC2 and ISO docs after this meeting
[05:33] Priya Patel: do logs include token-level data? we have PHI concerns
[05:38] Priya (Redwood): by default audit logs are metadata only (request id, route, model, latencies). you can enable more verbose logs for debug but redwood has full redaction options and we support no-log mode for sensitive workloads and bring-your-own-keys for encryption at rest
[06:00] Dr. Chen: good. on compliance, do you support SAML SSO and SCIM?
[06:05] Alex: yes SSO via SAML/OIDC and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC with granular roles is supported
[06:14] Priya: back to dashboards — here's a per-route trace view, you can click a spike and see sample requests, model version, prompt length distribution, and KV hits, gives you quick root cause for latency spikes
[06:36] Mark: sample requests — are prompts stored? where is PII stored?
[06:41] Priya: prompts are stored in ephemeral debug logs only if you opt-in; we default to truncated metadata storage and you can set retention or disable prompt logging; for PII we recommend no-log mode and private deployment
[06:58] Dr. Chen: can we tag traffic by customer-id? we have multi-tenant inside a route
[07:03] Priya: yes you can pass route-level tags/metadata and dashboards will group by tag; you can also create custom slices for billing or quota enforcement
[07:18] Alex: quick note on quotas — per-route quotas are enforced at the gateway; you can set soft and hard limits and the console surfaces quota usage with alerting hooks
[07:33] Dr. Chen: alerting — do you integrate with PagerDuty and Slack?
[07:36] Priya: yep webhooks, PagerDuty, Slack, and Datadog are supported out of box
[07:50] Mark: on performance, what kernels are you using — wondering about sequence length optimizations?
[07:57] Priya: our runtime chooses kernels based on model architecture and typical seq_len, and we have optimizations for attention patterns; that shows up in the model profile tab where you can see throughput and latency curves by seq_len
[08:18] Dr. Chen: how do you model batching tradeoffs? sometimes batching helps cost but hurts p95
[08:23] Priya: console has a batching simulator; you can toggle target latency SLO and it will show recommended batching config and expected cost delta; there's also an Optimize suggestions panel with recommended quantization and batching for a route
[08:45] Priya Patel: curious about end-to-end numbers — can you show example for our triage-assist route?
[08:50] Priya: sure, demoing a sample: triage-assist currently 500 qpm, avg prompt len 180 tokens, model redwood-17b-q4 with a per-token cost of $0.00012 in hosted, we estimate $X per 1k requests, and with prefix caching enabled we save ~28%
[09:18] Dr. Chen: what's the X?
[09:20] Priya: (laughs) sorry placeholder, in a real export you'll get exact dollar numbers — let me export CSV live
[09:30] [09:30] Priya: exported CSV and sharing link in chat: https://redwood.ai/share/exports/triage-assist-sample.csv (demo link)
[09:45] Mark: does CSV include model version breakdown? we need the finance chargeback per model
[09:50] Priya: yes includes model, route, tokens, cost components, and tags if you included them in requests
[10:02] Dr. Chen: any nuance around Dedicated — is there an infra surcharge?
[10:07] Alex: Dedicated has a reserved capacity fee and a lower per-token compute cost but there's an infra surcharge to cover reserved GPU and management; the console shows blended cost and an amortized infra line item
[10:23] Mark: ok for our POC we'd probably do Dedicated for triage-assist and Hosted for patient-summary to compare
[10:30] Priya: that works well; you can pin a route to Dedicated in the UI and the routing policy will ensure only that route uses dedicated pools
[10:42] Dr. Chen: about benchmarks, can Redwood run a 1h perf run against our staging traffic? we want to validate p95 at 1k qps
[10:50] Alex: yes we offer assisted benchmarks, we can schedule lab time with SE and infra. we'll need a sample traffic file and expected SLOs
[10:59] Priya: i'll attach a benchmark runbook and example traf file after, and we can coordinate a 1h run during dedicated window
[11:08] Mark: one more question — how granular are the dashboards for anomalies? say we have a spike for one customer at 3am
[11:14] Priya: there's anomaly detection that looks at historical baselines per-route and per-tag; when it flags a spike you can pivot to affected requests and see top tokens and KV hit changes
[11:30] Dr. Chen: perfect. next steps?
[11:33] Alex: recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO, pricing and T-shirt sizing sheet for Dedicated, priya will share csv export and runbook, halo to send expected traffic and confirm POC KPIs by 3/10, schedule POC kickoff for week of 3/12
[11:50] Mark: yep we'll sync internally and mark tentative 3/12, thanks everyone
[11:55] Alex: thanks all, will follow up with docs and calendar invite

Notes: occasional transcription errors (e.g., 'KV cashe' instead of KV cache, product names sometimes shortened). Links shared in chat during call: export CSV link (demo), metrics API sample.
